title: My Daily Routine
text: I wake up at seven o'clock. I eat breakfast. I drink coffee and eat bread. Then, I go to work. I work in an office. I finish work at five o'clock. In the evening, I watch television and go to bed at ten o'clock.

title: Booking a Hotel
text: Good morning, I would like to book a room for two nights, please. Do you have a double room available for this weekend? Yes, we do. It costs fifty pounds per night. Does that include breakfast? title: Climate Change Report
text: A new scientific report released today highlights the accelerating impact of climate change on coastal regions. The study indicates that sea levels are rising at a rate faster than previously predicted, threatening major cities worldwide. The primary driver remains the increased emission of greenhouse gases from industrial activities. Experts urge immediate international cooperation to transition to renewable energy sources and mitigate the impending environmental crisis.

What do experts recommend?

title: Philosophical Debate
text: The debate between determinism and free will has occupied philosophers for centuries. If the universe is governed by strict physical laws, and every event is the inevitable result of preceding causes, then human choices appear to be merely illusions. Conversely, the subjective experience of making autonomous decisions is profoundly compelling. Compatibilists attempt to reconcile this dichotomy by suggesting that free will is not the ability to do otherwise, but rather the capacity to act in accordance with one's own desires and motivations, unimpeded by external coercion.

questions.question: What does determinism imply about human choices?
How do compatibilists view free will?
options: As the ability to defy physical laws
As acting according to one's desires without coercion
As an inevitable result of preceding causes
